coverage: 19 proposed identities; conservative named bindings, contextual family titles, paragraph-end relationship gates. Bare ambiguous names, pronouns and generic titles are not exhaustive.

entities.name: Mr. Lockwood
entities.subtitle: The visiting tenant
entities.body: He rents Thrushcross Grange and calls on his landlord at Wuthering Heights. His account begins with his own impressions of the place.

entities.name: Mrs. Dean
entities.subtitle: The housekeeper at the Grange
entities.body: Lockwood turns to the housekeeper for company and information about his neighbours.

snapshots.name: Ellen “Nelly” Dean
snapshots.body: She grew up at Wuthering Heights alongside the Earnshaw children. Her history of the household includes events in which she took part, as well as things she witnessed.

entities.name: Heathcliff
entities.subtitle: Lockwood’s landlord
entities.body: He owns the house Lockwood rents. Lockwood admires his reserve on their first meeting, though Heathcliff offers him little welcome.

snapshots.name: Heathcliff
snapshots.body: Mr. Earnshaw brought him home from Liverpool as a child with no known family. Heathcliff is his whole name. Nelly recalls his friendship with Catherine and Hindley’s hostility; his ancestry remains unknown.

entities.name: Catherine Earnshaw
entities.subtitle: A name in the old bedroom
entities.body: Lockwood finds this name scratched on the ledge of a bed enclosed with wooden panels. Its repetition draws his attention to the room’s earlier occupant.

snapshots.name: Catherine Earnshaw
snapshots.body: Her name appears in an old book and on the window ledge. Lockwood dreams of a child calling herself Catherine Linton at the window; his account does not establish a supernatural event.

snapshots.name: Catherine Earnshaw
snapshots.body: The elder Catherine is Hindley’s sister, a child in the Earnshaw household. She is distinct from the young Mrs. Heathcliff whom Lockwood meets.

snapshots.name: Catherine Earnshaw
snapshots.body: The elder Catherine marries Edgar Linton and becomes Mrs. Linton. Nelly describes her attachment to Heathcliff alongside her wish for the position Edgar offers.

entities.name: Mrs. Heathcliff
entities.subtitle: The young woman at the Heights
entities.body: Lockwood addresses the young woman at the house as Mrs. Heathcliff. He has not yet understood her place in the household.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Heathcliff
snapshots.body: She is Heathcliff’s daughter-in-law and his son’s widow. Lockwood’s guesses that she is the wife of Heathcliff or of the young man beside him are mistaken.

snapshots.name: Catherine Linton
snapshots.body: Nelly identifies the young widow as Catherine Linton, her late master’s daughter and her former charge. She is distinct from the Catherine whose name Lockwood found in the bedroom.

snapshots.name: Catherine Linton
snapshots.body: The younger Catherine is the daughter of Edgar Linton and Catherine Earnshaw. Nelly recounts her birth and her mother’s death as separate lives in the same household.

entities.name: Hindley Earnshaw
entities.subtitle: The master in Catherine’s diary
entities.body: Catherine’s diary names Hindley as the person ruling the household in her father’s absence. She describes his treatment of Heathcliff as atrocious.

snapshots.name: Hindley Earnshaw
snapshots.body: Hindley is the elder Catherine’s brother and Hareton’s father. Nelly grew up alongside him and recalls the household under his father, Mr. Earnshaw.

entities.name: Hareton Earnshaw
entities.subtitle: The young man at the Heights
entities.body: He gives Lockwood his name angrily after the visitor has repeatedly guessed his position in the household incorrectly.

snapshots.name: Hareton Earnshaw
snapshots.body: Hareton is Hindley Earnshaw’s son. The young man Lockwood meets is a separate person from the name on the house’s carving dated 1500.

snapshots.name: Hareton Earnshaw
snapshots.body: Hareton is Hindley and Frances’s son. Nelly cares for him as a baby after Frances dies; he and the adult whom Lockwood meets are the same person.

entities.name: Edgar Linton
entities.subtitle: A boy at Thrushcross Grange
entities.body: Heathcliff describes seeing Edgar in the Grange’s comfortable drawing room with his sister. Their quarrel over a little dog attracts the watching children’s contempt.

snapshots.name: Edgar Linton
snapshots.body: Edgar, Isabella’s brother, marries Catherine Earnshaw. He belongs to the Linton family at Thrushcross Grange.

entities.name: Isabella Linton
entities.subtitle: Edgar’s sister
entities.body: She is one of the children Heathcliff watches through the drawing-room window at Thrushcross Grange. His hostile description comes from outside her household.

snapshots.name: Isabella Linton
snapshots.body: Isabella has married Heathcliff. Her note to Edgar asks for remembrance and reconciliation, but receives no reply. Her married title, Mrs. Heathcliff, also belongs to a different woman in Lockwood’s opening visits.

snapshots.name: Isabella Linton
snapshots.body: After leaving Wuthering Heights, Isabella settles near London and gives birth to a son named Linton. She describes the child as sickly in her correspondence with Edgar.

entities.name: Linton
entities.subtitle: The child named in Isabella’s letters
entities.body: Nelly recounts Isabella’s life away from the neighbourhood and the naming of her child.

snapshots.name: Linton Heathcliff
snapshots.body: Linton is Isabella and Heathcliff’s son. Linton is his given name; he is distinct from his uncle Edgar Linton and from his father Heathcliff.

entities.name: Joseph
entities.subtitle: A servant at Wuthering Heights
entities.body: Heathcliff calls on Joseph to take Lockwood’s horse. Lockwood finds the elderly servant sour and unwelcoming.

entities.name: Frances
entities.subtitle: A woman in Catherine’s diary
entities.body: Catherine’s account places Frances beside the man commanding the children. She joins in his rough treatment of Heathcliff.

snapshots.name: Frances
snapshots.body: Frances is Hindley’s wife. Catherine’s diary describes her pulling Heathcliff’s hair at Hindley’s request and then sitting on her husband’s knee.

snapshots.name: Frances Earnshaw
snapshots.body: Frances is Hareton’s mother. Nelly recounts her illness and death after his birth; little is known of her family before she married Hindley.

entities.name: Mr. Earnshaw
entities.subtitle: The elder Earnshaw
entities.body: Nelly recalls the older master of Wuthering Heights setting off on foot for Liverpool.

snapshots.name: Mr. Earnshaw
snapshots.body: He is Hindley and the elder Catherine’s father. Nelly remembers his promises of presents before a journey to Liverpool.

snapshots.name: Mr. Earnshaw
snapshots.body: He brings a homeless child back from Liverpool and raises him in the household as Heathcliff. His care for the child does not establish biological parentage.

entities.name: Mrs. Earnshaw
entities.subtitle: The elder Mrs. Earnshaw
entities.body: She waits with the children for Mr. Earnshaw to return from his journey to Liverpool.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Earnshaw
snapshots.body: She is the mother of Hindley and the elder Catherine. Nelly recalls her anger when her husband brings the unknown child home. She is distinct from Hindley’s wife Frances.

entities.name: Mr. Linton
entities.subtitle: The elder Linton
entities.body: He belongs to the older generation at Thrushcross Grange. Heathcliff’s account places the children in the drawing room while the adults are absent.

snapshots.name: Mr. Linton
snapshots.body: He is Edgar and Isabella’s father, a magistrate at Thrushcross Grange. In Heathcliff’s account he treats the unknown boy as a potential criminal. He is distinct from his son Edgar.

entities.name: Mrs. Linton
entities.subtitle: The elder Mrs. Linton
entities.body: She belongs to the older generation at Thrushcross Grange, where Heathcliff and Catherine watch the children through a window.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Linton
snapshots.body: She is Edgar and Isabella’s mother, addressed by her husband as Mary. She is distinct from Catherine Earnshaw, who also bears the title Mrs. Linton later in the account.

entities.name: Mr. Kenneth
entities.subtitle: The local doctor
entities.body: Kenneth is the medical practitioner consulted by the household. His opinions reach the reader through Nelly’s account.

entities.name: Zillah
entities.subtitle: A servant at the Heights
entities.body: She comes to Lockwood’s aid after his encounter with the dogs. She serves at Wuthering Heights, a different household from Mrs. Dean’s at the Grange.

entities.name: Mr. Shielders
entities.subtitle: The curate
entities.body: Mr. Linton names Shielders while criticising the children’s upbringing. He is the parish curate, distinct from the preacher in Lockwood’s dream.
